proposal.thesis: Phillips 66 is a refining-margin leader holding near its high while the momentum/software factor unwinds, so it diversifies a book whose risk is in NOW and NTRA. The margin backdrop is current and measurable: the EIA's 2026-10-05 note shows Q3 distillate and jet crack spreads almost tripled year over year with U.S. distillate inventories 13% below the five-year average as of 9/25, and PSX printed a $41.63/bbl Q2 composite crack with 98% market capture and guided 95% capture for Q3. Live $292.89 is 2.8% under the 52-week high (~$301) in a weekly uptrend above the 50/200-DMA with ADX 32.6. My measured move is a break of the ~$301 high toward $325 (+10.5% from the $294 entry cap) as winter distillate tightness extends the margin cycle into Q4. This is an honest 0.54 probe, not a full-size entry, because the stock is extended (weekly RSI 78.4) and the Q3 windfall is consensus.
catalysts: Weekly EIA distillate inventory reports (Wednesdays) through late October
Peer VLO Q3 print 2026-10-22 bmo as a read-through on Q4 crack commentary
PSX Q3 earnings 2026-10-28 bmo with Q4 capture and turnaround guidance
proposal.macro_context: Neutral regime (3/5) with SPY above its 200-DMA, but the 10y at 5.19% and rising is pressuring long-duration growth, and a coded momentum unwind is hitting software. Energy and refiners are the groups being bid in that rotation, and the book's holdings correlate near zero with each other (avg pairwise -0.03), so a refiner adds a different return stream rather than more duration risk.
proposal.risk_map: What kills it: a diplomatic breakthrough that reopens Hormuz or a fast rebuild of distillate stocks that collapses cracks, or a 10/28 print where capture slips well below the 95% guide or Q4 commentary flags margin normalization. Early warnings: distillate inventories rebuilding toward the five-year average in the weekly EIA data, VLO's 10/22 call guiding Q4 cracks down, or PSX losing $285 while energy peers hold.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: the street expects a Q3 windfall above the near-record Q2 for VLO, MPC and PSX, the shares are near highs after roughly +124% in a year, and Zacks carries PSX at Rank #1 with estimates rising, so the quarter itself is priced. MY VIEW: the market is treating this as a one-quarter spike to fade after the print, but the Q4 margin run-rate stays elevated because distillate is the tightest product heading into winter heating demand. MECHANISM: sell-side models typically mean-revert cracks within a quarter or two, yet U.S. distillate stocks are 13% below the five-year average with Russia, China and Middle East supply disrupted and PSX's own management saying the shortage may last longer than 2022, so forward estimates are too low on Q4/Q1 cracks rather than on Q3. RESOLUTION: VLO's 10/22 call and PSX's 10/28 Q4 capture and crack commentary, plus weekly EIA distillate data through October.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_print: The 10/28 Q3 print shows refining capture well below the 95% guide or management guides Q4 crack/capture down on normalizing distillate supply; or weekly EIA data show distillate stocks back near the five-year average before then.
thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A daily close below $279 (the stop), or a close back under $285 while CVX/VLO hold their levels, which would be stock-specific failure rather than a sector washout.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If PSX has not closed above $301 (the 52-week high) by 2026-10-30, two sessions after the print, exit; the breakout thesis will have failed to resolve.
